thread:
Priya: Heads up — since the kernel-selector tweak last night we're seeing 95th token-latency spikes for several private/VPC customers. Pattern looks like lots of short requests with heavy KV cache misses.
Alex: Which metric? can you paste a chart or numbers?
Priya: 95p token latency went from ~12ms -> ~58ms for route /v1/generate-prod. Per-token breakdown shows jump in compute + wait_for_kernel.
Priya: sample metrics:
```
redwood_token_latency_seconds{route="/v1/generate-prod",quantile="0.95"} 0.058
redwood_token_latency_components_seconds{stage="kv_fetch",route="/v1/generate-prod",quantile="0.95"} 0.022
redwood_token_latency_components_seconds{stage="kernel_lock",route="/v1/generate-prod",quantile="0.95"} 0.012
redwood_token_latency_components_seconds{stage="compute",route="/v1/generate-prod",quantile="0.95"} 0.018
```
Jordan: hmm looks like kernel_lock + kv_fetch add up. Did the selector start preferring fallback kernels that can't use local KVCACHE?
Priya: Exactly. Selector picks fallback (int8) when seq_len small; that variant currently routes to a separate runner w/ cold KV warmup. In hosted we warm caches, but VPC private runners don't prefetch.
Sandeep: For VPC customers we should either: 1) avoid fallback kernel for small seqs, 2) enable async kv warmup, or 3) expose perf tag to routing so dedupe fewer migrations.
Alex: Agreed. Also noticed our Prometheus exporter in VPC wasn't sending component-level histograms because of label cardinality filter — customer-side scrape rules trimmed them.
Priya: Right — config in the private exporter had `drop_labels: ["component"]` set by default in 1.2.0 to reduce cardinality. We need to revert or add a per-route toggle.
Jordan: Short-term fix: change batching heuristic to coalesce tiny requests for same route for 200ms window. Might clamp median batch size up.
Sandeep: Can we push a small probe exporter that writes local metrics to disk and allows air-gapped customers to pull? Customer security requires no outgoing connections.
Priya: idea: export to file in /var/lib/redwood/metrics-latest.prom and add an operator tool to securely fetch via customer-initiated scp.
Alex: Security ok w/ infra if annotated. But we need to ensure token-level histograms are included. Also add an example Grafana panel config (json) for token breakdown.
Priya: I'll open a PR with: (1) revert drop_labels default, (2) batching heuristic tweak, (3) file-export probe + docs. Also will attach sample dashboards and perf regression test.
Jordan: please include a small perf eval harness so we can run locally against private runners.
Priya: Will do. @Sandeep can you validate airgap scp workflow with docs team? :eyes: 
Sandeep: On it. I'll coordinate with support to notify affected customers.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: eng-runtime/revert-drop_labels + batching-probe -> canary (eta 12m)
Alex: Thanks. Keep us posted.
